correctness.rationale: For the 96 length-four words of GC-content two, exactly 72 satisfy the self reverse-complement restriction. The direct constrained compatibility graph has 1,168 undirected edges, and the ordinary distance-three graph has 3,312 edges. Complete maximal-clique enumeration independently gives constrained clique number six with 512 labeled maximum cliques and ordinary clique number twelve with 128 labeled maximum cliques. Of the latter, 16 are reverse-complement invariant, eight contain no fixed words, and each of those eight contains exactly six complement pairs with all 64 transversals valid. The stated 256 transformations preserve the constrained graph and have four code orbits, each of size 128. These finite checks enumerate the entire finite parameter space rather than sample from it.

limitations: All enumerations concern length four, GC-content two, and distance three; no generalization to longer sequences or alternative DNA constraints is claimed.
Finite enumeration is exhaustive only because the entire 96-word ambient set and both graphs are enumerated.
The order-256 action is a specified constraint-preserving subgroup; no assertion is made that it is the entire automorphism group.

evidence: King 2003 Theorem 7 establishes the halving bound A^{GC,RC}<=A^{GC}/2.

Chee–Ling 2008 Table I lists numbers of maximum cliques only for constrained (5,3,2), (5,4,2), (6,4,3), (7,5,3), (7,6,3) and weak (5,3,2), (6,5,3), not (4,3,2).
Gaborit–King 2005 describes linear/additive constructions and parameter tables; full text was not accessible in this assessment.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Extremal size bounds and constructions can coexist with many different equality layers. The earlier general halving theorem implies the 12-word closure of every size-6 optimizer but does not determine how many parent optima are reverse-complement invariant, how many are viable, or the number and orbits of transversals. The inaccessible 2005 full text is retained as priority risk rather than declared not covering.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The former result implies the parent map and its maximum cardinality, but not the parent classification nor 8-by-64 count; the parent-transversal argument plus the complete ordinary graph enumeration supply the missing information. The orbit formula additionally depends on a checked order-256 action and is not entailed by known scalar optima.

originality.rationale: The known optimum 6 and the ordinary optimum 12 are not new. The surviving exact claim is the complete labeled equality census, the reverse-complement-invariant ordinary-parent classification, and the orbit decomposition under the explicitly stated order-256 action. King 2003 supplies only parameterwise optimal cardinalities; Chee–Ling 2008 enumerates maximum cliques at other parameters. No inspected complete source states this equality census. Full text of Gaborit–King 2005 remains a priority uncertainty.
residual_risks: The full Gaborit–King 2005 and Aboluion–Smith–Perkins 2012 papers were not materially inspected; an equality-case appendix remains possible.
Unindexed or obscure finite-census tables could contain the numerical classification under another equivalence convention.
The orbit decomposition is explicitly relative to the specified order-256 symmetry subgroup, not asserted for the full automorphism group of the compatibility graph.

value.rationale: The (n,d,w)=(4,3,2) cell is a natural smallest sharp test of the classical constant-GC reverse-complement halving bound. The equality classification reveals exactly which ordinary optima induce admissible reverse-complement codes and exhausts the labeled and symmetry-reduced maxima. It is a structural refinement beyond the already known optimal cardinality, not a purported improvement to bounds.
